releases.body:
* **Local AI Test tolerates a cold model.** The probe now waits up to 60 s: the
  first call after a download loads the model from disk (tens of seconds), and a
  15 s timeout reported a working model as offline.

### Local AI: a small local model for bounded work

* New **Settings → Local AI** card: enable a local model (Ollama, LM Studio,
  vLLM — any OpenAI-compatible endpoint), choose the download policy (`auto`
  pulls through Ollama, `manual` prints the exact command), watch a pull with
  progress, and test the endpoint. Off by default; every consumer falls back to
  the previous behaviour when the model or runtime is unavailable.
* `perun/local_llm.py` is the only client: stdlib transport, an 8 s timeout,
  JSON-mode fallback for runtimes that reject `response_format`, a cached health
  probe, and it never raises. `perun/model_manager.py` drives Ollama
  (`/api/tags`, `/api/pull`, `/api/delete`) with a disk guard, one pull at a
  time, cancellation, and persisted job progress.
* Consumers: the changelog bullet after an executed proposal (shadow mode logs
  the locally generated line instead of using it) and OpenCode's own
  `small_model` for titles/small tasks (written through the backed-up config
  writer, removed when the toggle is turned off).
* New **Settings → Context** card: opt-in boundary compaction through OpenCode's
  `POST /session/{id}/compact`. It triggers on the live context size, respects a
  cooldown in messages, never touches an active session, records before/after
  rows, and disables itself when three compactions fail to shrink the context.
* Search and memory tools cap their output (`context_tool_budget_chars`,
  `context_memory_budget_chars`) with an explicit truncation marker; exact file
  reads are never truncated.
* Schema v27 adds `local_ai_jobs` and `context_events`.

* The VS Code companion package now ships its MIT license
  (`extensions/vscode/LICENSE`), so `vsce` no longer warns and the installed
  extension carries the license text.

* **Windows: paths with cmd metacharacters.** `_code_command()` quoted an
  argument only when it contained a space, so a VSIX under a path like
  `C:\R&D\…` was split at the `&` and `code` reported
  `Extension 'c:\…\perun' not found`. Every argument is now quoted; verified
  live with a `perun&co` directory.
* **Download validation is total.** The packaged manifest must be ≤ 1 MB
  (`ZipInfo.file_size`, so a zip bomb never expands into memory), and any decode
  failure — encryption, unsupported compression, truncation — is treated as
  "not the companion" instead of raising out of `perun install`.
* The `publish-companion` job runs the extension unit tests before it publishes,
  `perun install` no longer touches VS Code when the global install failed, and
  `--no-vscode-download` no longer claims a `--vscode` flag that does not exist.

### Windows: the companion install survives paths with spaces

* `install_vscode_extension()` passed `["cmd.exe", "/c", …]` to
  `subprocess.run`, which `cmd.exe` re-parses and de-quotes. With both the
  `code.cmd` shim (`…\Microsoft VS Code\…`) and the VSIX under a path with a
  space (a user name or install directory), it stripped the quotes and failed
  with `'…\Microsoft' is not recognized as an internal or external command`.
  The line is now wrapped in the extra quote pair `cmd.exe /c` expects, and a
  regression test pins it.

### Companion distribution hardening

* The VSIX is published by its own `publish-companion` workflow job, so a
  failing Windows or macOS installer build can no longer leave the release
  without a downloadable companion (that is how v0.14.2 shipped nothing).
* A downloaded VSIX must contain `extension/package.json` for
  `perun`/`perun-overseer`; a proxy page or a foreign archive is refused and
  never written to disk.
* `perun install` is a no-op when `code --list-extensions --show-versions`
  already reports the VSIX version (`--force` reinstalls), and
  `--no-vscode-download` restricts it to a local VSIX for offline installs.
* The Windows installer no longer copies the VSIX twice (`installer\vscode` is
  excluded from the recursive copy; the file is still installed to
  `{app}\vscode`), and `AGENTS.md` records that the companion is per-user and
  never installs VS Code.

### Release packaging: the companion actually ships

* `npm run package` creates `installer/vscode/` before asking `vsce` to write
  the VSIX. The directory is gitignored and therefore absent in a fresh clone,
  so the release workflow died with `ENOENT` at the packaging step: **v0.14.2
  published no GitHub release at all**, and v0.14.1 shipped only the macOS
  `.pkg` (no `PerunSetup.exe`).
* Every GitHub release now attaches `perun-overseer.vsix` next to the
  installers, so source, command-line and Linux installations can install the
  companion without building it.
* `python -m perun install` (and `--machine`) installs the companion for the
  current user when VS Code is present — from a local VSIX or the release asset —
  and reports a clear "skipped" line when VS Code, the network, or a per-user
  install is unavailable. `--skip-vscode` opts out.
* `installer/build.ps1` builds the companion (when npm is available) before
  compiling the setup executable, and says so loudly instead of silently
  shipping an installer without it.

### Dashboard presence refresh

* **Working now** keeps its 4 s poll, gains a **Refresh** button, and refreshes
  immediately when the dashboard tab becomes visible or the window regains
  focus. A closed TUI disappears on the next poll instead of waiting for a page
  reload; if it lingers, the server still considers the run active and the
  reconcile sweep will finalize it.

### Accurate usage across every message and provider

* `opencode_api.usage()` now follows OpenCode's `cursor.next` across **all**
  session pages (the API caps one page at 200 messages). A single 200-message
  page had silently undercounted long TUI sessions: one real session stored
  **$0.59** while its full history was **$123.50** (including $108.51 of
  `ollama-cloud/kimi-k3.1-pro`). An expired cursor restarts the walk once from
  the newest page; message ids keep the retry idempotent.
* Snapshots record `usage_complete`, `usage_pages` and `usage_messages`; the
  `/api/usage` totals expose an `incomplete` count and project-scoped
  per-provider/per-model breakdowns.
* Starting a new TUI from the dashboard creates the OpenCode session first and
  passes its id to the TUI, so the run is attributable from the first message.
  Older TUI runs bind to the single active session or the single session created
  after the run started.
* `POST /api/usage/refresh` is single-flight, re-reads recent sessions
  (repairing pre-pagination snapshots), and the dashboard Usage card has a
  refresh button plus a **partial** badge.

### VS Code: macOS companion install and explicit workspace files

* The macOS `.pkg` postinstall installs `perun-overseer.vsix` for the console
  user when VS Code and its `code` CLI are present (still never installs VS Code
  itself).
* `vscode/open` no longer generates a workspace file as a side effect of opening
  a folder. It opens the project folder by default; `workspace_file: true`
  explicitly creates/opens the `.code-workspace`.
* New **Perun: Open TUI (tracked)** command in the companion (Command Palette):
  it creates a TUI run through Perun and opens/focuses the same tracked OpenCode
  terminal in the current VS Code window.
* Terminal bindings are persisted in `workspaceState` and re-reported on
  activation and every `hello.ok`; Focus/Stop survive a Perun restart or a
  VS Code reload. The server rejects a protocol mismatch, and the Config panel
  shows the companion version/connected windows plus the real VSIX install
  command (extension 0.1.4).
* **Perun: Open TUI (tracked)** / the **Perun TUI** status item shows the same
  session choice as the dashboard Run caret: resume latest, pick a recent
  session, or start new; a terminal already open for that session is focused.
* The companion adds two status-bar items: **Perun** opens the dashboard directly
  in VS Code's **Simple Browser** tab (short-lived embed ticket; no wrapper page
  or extra click) and re-focuses an existing Perun tab when it can; **Perun TUI**
  opens a session picker (resume latest / choose a recent session / new) and then
  the tracked OpenCode terminal. The TUI opens beside the editor (wide), waits
  150 ms for the pty size, and resumes the chosen session. Extension 0.1.4.
* Run-completion fallback: if a TUI run produced no live file event (e.g. a tool
  schema change), changed files from `git status` are revealed once at close or
  Finish. Stale terminal bindings are dropped on disconnect, the per-file
  debounce cache is pruned, the in-project `.git/info/exclude` entry is removed
  on unlink, and the extension log is capped at 1 MB.

### VS Code: open the folder, not an untrusted workspace file

* `POST /api/projects/{slug}/vscode/open` now opens the project **folder** by
  default. A generated `.code-workspace` is a new VS Code trust scope and opens in
  Restricted Mode, which disables the companion; the folder inherits the user's
  existing trust. The workspace file stays opt-in (`workspace_file: true`).
* The companion retries while the project is not registered yet, instead of
  staying offline until a manual reconnect (extension 0.1.1).
* Removed the unauthenticated `GET .../vscode/context` endpoint: selection text
  can contain secrets and must not be readable by any local GET caller.

### VS Code deep integration

* Link any project to a generated `.code-workspace` from the wizard, project card
  or Config panel. Linked projects show a badge and an **Open in VS Code** action.
* Two launch modes: host the TUI in VS Code's integrated terminal (seamless
  `@file#lines` selection insertion) or keep the external terminal while VS Code
  follows edits. A per-run override is available from the Run caret.
* Live edit following: the global OpenCode event stream is mapped to a project,
  validated against the project root, debounced and sent to the companion for
  reveal + highlight. Without the companion, linked projects fall back to
  `code --reuse-window --goto`.
* Companion extension (`perun.perun-overseer`): status bar, ticket-authenticated
  loopback WebSocket, selection command (`Ctrl+Alt+P`), terminal open/focus/close,
  and `terminal.processId` binding so Stop/Focus keep working.
* Security: single-use workspace-bound tickets, no long-lived token in a URL,
  fixed message schema, loopback-only endpoints, ignored workspace-level
  `perun.*` settings, path validation, and no silent VS Code install.
* VSIX is built in the release workflow and installed per-user by the Windows
  installer; the dashboard reports a missing/outdated companion.

### Documentation refresh

* `README.md` and `docs/DESIGN.md` now describe the Telegram card grammar,
  coloured buttons, live run drafts and per-chat message scheduling;
  `AGENTS_OPTIMIZATION.md` and the Shared Projects PRD name v0.13.3.

### Telegram bridge: finish the audit follow-ups

* The run path now joins the live-draft thread (up to 1 s) before sending the
  final answer, so an in-flight draft update cannot leave a stale "Working…"
  preview after the reply. Tool events obey the same 1.6 s throttle.
* `setMyCommands` uses `retries=1` at startup, so an outage cannot delay the
  poller by the full retry budget.
* Plain messages from different chats now run concurrently (one run per chat),
  so a long agent run in one chat no longer blocks messages from another. The
  durable queue still delivers per-chat updates in order.
* `format_html()` strips NUL bytes before inserting private placeholders, so
  agent text containing a literal placeholder can no longer corrupt output.
